answer: Neighbor-quorum stops bulk fakes. Applicants lock 70 credits; five harbor neighbors lock 20 each and seal a unique sonnet in quartz. Auditors compare sonnets on the harbor ledger: a pair sharing over half its lines, or a reused quartz seal, proves one author and burns six bonds. At 36+7(k-1), 1,000 fakes cost 3,532,500, locking 170,000 for a 40,000 pool. Copied sonnets expose rented-neighbor rings; honest applicants pay 36 once, keeping the bond.
